clue.text: Only half of stores getting prompt delivery

indicators.note: taking only half of a word means keeping one end of it and dropping the rest

blocks.note: the back half of the six-letter word
a prompt to an actor is a cue

explanation.surface: A shop gets only half of its prompt delivery of stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delivery' in the surface is a shipment of goods; as the definition it is a delivery from danger.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliver someone from harm is to save them, so deliverance or salvation is a rescue.

clue.text: Play shot with cue — it features down under

definitions.note: the answer is a plural noun naming things that feature in Australia

indicators.note: shot means ruined or wrecked, so the letters are broken up and reassembled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A snooker player plays a shot with a cue Down Under.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play shot' reads as a snooker stroke, but play is fodder and shot is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Eucalypti, the gum trees, are everywhere in the Australian landscape, a defining feature of the country.

clue.text: See nothing out of place in examiner soothing singer

indicators.note: a letter out of place has been moved, so the word is rearranged

blocks.note: nothing is the letter O, which you will see in the wrong spot
a coroner examines the causes of sudden deaths

explanation.surface: Nothing seems amiss when an inspector turns into a gentle vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: Only one O moves: shift the second letter of the examiner along one place.
explanation.definitionFit: A crooner sings sentimental songs in a soft, smooth style that calms the listener.

clue.text: Lady's formal greeting reflected

indicators.note: a reflection is a mirror image, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: Ave is Latin for hail, a formal salutation

explanation.surface: A woman's polite salutation is mirrored back to her.
explanation.definitionFit: Eva is a woman's first name, and a lady stands for any female name in crosswords.

clue.text: Individual emulates retiring judge

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the word before it is read backwards

blocks.note: to ape someone is to imitate them
to rate is to assess or judge

explanation.surface: Someone copies a judge who is stepping down from the bench.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Individual' is the adjective here, as in separate or distinct items.
explanation.definitionFit: Separate and individual both describe things that are distinct and treated one at a time.

clue.text: Promise son to be in

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
to be in a coat is to wear it

explanation.surface: A parent promises a son will be home.
explanation.definitionFit: To swear is to vow or give a solemn undertaking, a verb synonym of promise.

clue.text: A much-loved rogue journalist executed

blocks.note: a, as in so much a head, means per
a pet is a favourite
a rat is a scoundrel
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: A popular scoundrel of a reporter was put to death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Executed' means killed on the surface but means carried out in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To perpetrate a crime is to commit or carry it out, as executing a plan is carrying it out.

clue.text: Slightly overestimate assembly

blocks.note: first meaning: to take a figure to the next whole number above
second meaning: a gathering together, as of cattle or suspects

explanation.walkthrough: The first meaning is the two-word verb; the second is the hyphenated noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Rounding a number up nudges it a little higher, and a cattle roundup gathers animals together.

clue.text: Daily robbery?

blocks.note: a daily is a newspaper, here the Financial Times with its article in front

explanation.surface: A question about whether something happens every day.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as THE FT, a newspaper that comes out daily.
explanation.definitionFit: Theft is the act of stealing, which is what a robbery involves.

clue.text: Honour a rebel leader admitting heightened depression

indicators.note: admitting means letting something in, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: taken as written
Jack Cade led a rebellion in Kent in 1450
a col is a dip between mountain peaks, a low point found high up

explanation.surface: A revolutionary who is suffering a bout of elevated gloom is given an honour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depression' suggests low mood, but it is a geographic hollow; Jack Cade's rebellion is an English history staple.
explanation.definitionFit: An accolade is an award or mark of praise, the same thing as an honour.

clue.text: Runs remote IT equipment

blocks.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs
remote and outer both mean far out

explanation.surface: Someone operates computer gear from a distance.
explanation.definitionFit: A router is a networking device that directs data between computers, a piece of IT hardware.

clue.text: Constrained style of book, long dull volume with Gaelic appendix

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for book
lank hair is long, limp and lifeless
V is the abbreviation for volume
Erse is an old name for the Gaelic language
says the last piece is tacked on at the end

explanation.surface: A literary critic describes a long, boring tome with a Gaelic appendix.
explanation.walkthrough: Blank verse is unrhymed but held to a strict metre, which is why it can be called constrained.
explanation.definitionFit: Blank verse is a poetic form bound by iambic pentameter, a style of writing with formal restrictions.

clue.text: Mild avarice troubled leader in service

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so the letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: the letters as written

explanation.surface: A boss in public service is bothered by a bit of greed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' is one of the armed forces, here the navy.
explanation.definitionFit: A vice admiral is a senior naval officer, a commander in one of the armed services.

clue.text: Assess age of fruit

blocks.note: first meaning: to establish how old something is
second meaning: the sweet fruit of a palm

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as judging how ripe some fruit is; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the verb for working out a time of origin and a palm tree's brown fruit.

clue.text: Mineral box

blocks.note: first meaning: a crystalline mineral, as in feldspar
second meaning: to box lightly, as in training

explanation.walkthrough: 'Box' looks like a container of minerals, but it is the verb for fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a light-coloured crystalline rock and also means to practise boxing with a partner.

clue.text: Virtual realm PC creates by expressing time irregularly

indicators.note: to express is literally to press out, so the following letter is squeezed out
irregular means out of order, so the remaining letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters as written
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A computer conjures up a virtual world by working out time unevenly.
explanation.walkthrough: One T is removed from the fodder before the rest is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyberspace is the notional environment of online communication, a world that exists only virtually.

clue.text: Buddhist's heading for one to pray

indicators.note: a heading sits at the top, so only the opening letter is wanted

blocks.note: the opening letter
eg, for example, is what 'for one' means

explanation.surface: A Buddhist sets out to say a prayer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pray' is the old sense of please or entreat, not religious prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: To pray someone to do something is to beseech them, the same as to beg.

clue.text: Condemned in a second, as was Jeanne d'Arc

indicators.note: something condemned is wrecked or ruined, so the letters are broken and reassembled

blocks.note: the letters as written

explanation.surface: Joan of Arc was condemned in a flash.
explanation.walkthrough: Joan of Arc was burned for heresy in 1431, then made a saint in 1920, so 'Condemned' fits the surface story exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: Joan of Arc was officially declared a saint by the Catholic Church, which is what canonised means.

clue.text: Frantic detectives directed across river

indicators.note: one piece lies across another, straddling it so the other sits within

blocks.note: DIs are Detective Inspectors
to direct can mean to instruct
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Panicking police officers are sent over a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Distraught describes someone deeply upset and agitated, the same state as frantic.

clue.text: Propose carrying Times article, subject to official charges

indicators.note: carrying something means holding it within

blocks.note: to table a motion is to propose it
x is the multiplication sign
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone suggests running a newspaper piece about official levies.
explanation.definitionFit: Taxable income is liable to tax, a charge imposed by the authorities.

clue.text: Just less than a shilling to look after?

blocks.note: a shilling was twelve old pence, so just under it is ten pence, written as ten d

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a sum just short of a shilling to mind something.
explanation.walkthrough: Before 1971 British money had twelve pennies (d) to the shilling, so ten pence was 10d.
explanation.definitionFit: To tend a garden or a patient is to care for it, a synonym of look after.

clue.text: Upheaval due to stated limit on fossil fuel

indicators.note: stated means said out loud, so the word is spelt by how it sounds

blocks.note: a term is a fixed limit of time
oil is a fossil fuel

explanation.surface: Disruption follows a cap placed on oil and gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Limit on' tells you the limit sits before the fuel in a down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Turmoil is a state of great disturbance or confusion, as upheaval is.

clue.text: Cross US conflict zone returning from island

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the letters are read in the other direction

blocks.note: a cross is the letter X
'Nam is American slang for Vietnam in the war years

explanation.surface: A soldier is angry about coming home from a war zone to an island.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces are turned round together. The Isle of Man lies in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Manx is the adjective for things belonging to the Isle of Man, so coming from that island.

clue.text: Where Plato met commander gathering troops?

indicators.note: gathering means collecting in, so one piece is enclosed by the other

blocks.note: an aga is a Turkish military commander
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A question about where the philosopher met an officer mustering soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: The agora was the public square of ancient Athens, where philosophers met and debated.

clue.text: Convoluted message backing Communist blocks

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the word after it is read backwards
something that blocks a passage sits in the middle of it, splitting it

blocks.note: the meaning of something is its message
red is the traditional colour of communism

explanation.surface: A garbled message supports a Communist who obstructs things.
explanation.definitionFit: Meandering describes a winding, rambling course, much as convoluted means twisting and complicated.

clue.text: One who wrote poetry from a university hideaway

blocks.note: taken as written
U is the abbreviation for university
a den is a private retreat

explanation.surface: A writer composes poems in a campus retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: W H Auden was a major twentieth-century Anglo-American poet.

clue.text: Clothes, left out for Adelaide's friend

indicators.note: out means removed, so the letter named before it is dropped

blocks.note: clobber is British slang for clothes or gear
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Someone sets out clothing for a friend called Adelaide.
explanation.walkthrough: Adelaide is not a woman but the Australian city, so the definition asks for an Australian word.
explanation.definitionFit: Cobber is Australian slang for a mate or companion, the friend of someone from Adelaide.

clue.text: Right method introduced to smother rodent

indicators.note: something introduced to another is put inside it

blocks.note: to douse a fire is to put it out by smothering it
R is the abbreviation for right
MO is modus operandi, a method of working

explanation.surface: The correct technique is brought in to suffocate a pest.
explanation.definitionFit: The dormouse is a small sleepy rodent, a specific example of the general class.

clue.text: Go off tripe

blocks.note: first meaning: to decay or spoil
second meaning: nonsense

explanation.walkthrough: Tripe reads as offal that might spoil, but here it means rubbish talk.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to decompose, as food does, and worthless talk or nonsense.

clue.text: Strategy for playing softly in percussion group

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

blocks.note: a gamelan is an Indonesian percussion orchestra
p is the musical marking piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: A musician works out a plan for playing quietly within a drum ensemble.
explanation.definitionFit: A game plan is the planned approach a team or player takes, a strategy for how to play.

clue.text: Fine blade was first to pierce further

indicators.note: piercing something means passing into it, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: too means also, in addition
to have led a race is to have been first

explanation.surface: A sword cuts deeper than any before it.
explanation.walkthrough: Toledo in Spain was famous for its sword steel, so a fine sword can itself be called a Toledo.
explanation.definitionFit: A Toledo is a high-quality sword made in the Spanish city, so the name stands for a fine blade.
